metadata.title: Master Muscle & Exercise Anatomical Library
metadata.description: Consolidated, decoupled, relational anatomical muscle and exercise database

Abductor Hallucis & Flexor Digitorum Brevis stretch
Stretch for wrist and finger flexors
Shoulder lateral rotation with resistance band
Shoulder medial rotation with resistance band (keep elbow tucked in)
Kneeling reverse shoulder stretch (hands on table)

muscles.anatomical_region: Posterior Compartment of the Leg - Superficial Layer
muscles.latin_origin: gaster (stomach), kneme (lower leg)
muscles.origin: Medial head: posterior surface of distal femur just superior to medial condyle. Lateral head: upper posterolateral surface of lateral femoral condyle.
muscles.insertion: Posterior surface of calcaneus via the Achilles tendon.
muscles.action: Plantar flexes foot. Flexes knee. Main propelling force in walking and running.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Standing on tiptoes.
muscles.injury_risks: Achilles tendon strain or rupture, tennis leg (medial head strain).

muscles.anatomical_region: Posterior Compartment of the Leg - Superficial Layer
muscles.latin_origin: solea (leather sole/sandal/sole)
muscles.origin: Posterior aspect of fibular head and adjacent surfaces of neck and proximal shaft. Soleal line and medial border of tibia.
muscles.insertion: Posterior surface of calcaneus via the Achilles tendon.
muscles.action: Plantar flexes foot. Maintains upright posture by preventing body from falling forward at the ankle joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Standing on tiptoes.
muscles.injury_risks: Chronic overuse strains during long-distance endurance running.

muscles.anatomical_region: Posterior Compartment of the Leg - Superficial Layer
muscles.latin_origin: plantaris (relating to the sole)
muscles.origin: Lower part of lateral supracondylar line of femur and oblique popliteal ligament of knee joint.
muscles.insertion: Posterior surface of calcaneus via the Achilles tendon.
muscles.action: Plantar flexes foot. Flexes knee.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Standing on tiptoes.
muscles.injury_risks: Plantaris tendon rupture (often misdiagnosed as Achilles rupture).

muscles.anatomical_region: Posterior Compartment of the Leg - Intermediate Layer
muscles.latin_origin: flectere (to bend), digitorum (of the toes), longus (long)
muscles.origin: Medial side of posterior surface of tibia, below soleal line.
muscles.insertion: Plantar surfaces of bases of distal phalanges of lateral four toes.
muscles.action: Flexes lateral four toes (enables foot to firmly grip ground when walking).
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Pushing off the surface in walking, standing on tiptoes.
muscles.injury_risks: Over-pronation leading to flexor tendonitis.

muscles.anatomical_region: Posterior Compartment of the Leg - Intermediate Layer
muscles.latin_origin: flectere (to bend), hallucis (of the great toe), longus (long)
muscles.origin: Lower two-thirds of posterior surface of fibula and adjacent interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Plantar surface of base of distal phalanx of great toe.
muscles.action: Flexes great toe. Important in final propulsive thrust of foot during walking.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Pushing off the surface in walking, standing on tiptoes.
muscles.injury_risks: Dancer's tendinitis (FHL tendinopathy behind medial malleolus).

muscles.anatomical_region: Posterior Compartment of the Leg - Deep Layer
muscles.latin_origin: tibialis (relating to the shin), posterior (at the back)
muscles.origin: Posterior surfaces of interosseous membrane and adjacent regions of tibia and fibula.
muscles.insertion: Mainly to tuberosity of navicular and adjacent region of medial cuneiform.
muscles.action: Inverts and plantar flexes foot. Supports medial arch of foot during walking.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Standing on tiptoes, pushing down car pedals.
muscles.injury_risks: Repetitive impact leading to posterior tibial tendon dysfunction (PTTD).

muscles.anatomical_region: Posterior Compartment of the Leg - Deep Layer
muscles.latin_origin: poples (the ham)
muscles.origin: Lateral femoral condyle.
muscles.insertion: Posterior surface of proximal tibia.
muscles.action: Stabilizes and unlocks the knee joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Walking.
muscles.injury_risks: Sudden knee hyperextension or twisting injuries.

muscles.anatomical_region: Lateral Compartment of the Leg
muscles.latin_origin: fibula (pin/buckle), longus (long), brevis (short)
muscles.origin: Fibularis longus: upper two-thirds of lateral surface of fibula, head of fibula. Fibularis brevis: lower two-thirds of lateral surface of shaft of fibula.
muscles.insertion: Fibularis longus: lateral side of distal end of medial cuneiform, base of first metatarsal. Fibularis brevis: lateral tubercle at base of fifth metatarsal.
muscles.action: Fibularis longus: everts and plantar flexes foot, supports arches of foot. Fibularis brevis: everts foot.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Walking on uneven ground.
muscles.injury_risks: Inversion ankle sprains causing peroneal tendon strain or subluxation.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Sole of the Foot - First Layer
muscles.latin_origin: abducere (to lead away from), hallucis (of the great toe)
muscles.origin: Medial process of calcaneal tuberosity.
muscles.insertion: Medial side of base of proximal phalanx of great toe.
muscles.nerve: Medial plantar nerve from tibial nerve S1-3
muscles.action: Abducts and flexes great toe at metatarsophalangeal joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Helps foot stability and power in walking and running.
muscles.injury_risks: Foot arch collapse from unsupportive footwear.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Sole of the Foot - First Layer
muscles.latin_origin: flectere (to bend), digitorum (of toes), brevis (short)
muscles.origin: Medial process of calcaneal tuberosity and plantar aponeurosis.
muscles.insertion: Sides of plantar surfaces of middle phalanges of lateral four toes.
muscles.nerve: Medial plantar nerve from tibial nerve S1-3
muscles.action: Flexes lateral four toes at proximal interphalangeal joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Helps foot stability and power in walking and running.
muscles.injury_risks: Repetitive impact on hard surfaces.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Sole of the Foot - First Layer
muscles.latin_origin: abducere (to lead away from), digiti (of toe), minimi (smallest)
muscles.origin: Lateral and medial processes of calcaneal tuberosity, connective tissue band to base of fifth metatarsal.
muscles.insertion: Lateral side of base of proximal phalanx of little toe.
muscles.nerve: Lateral plantar nerve from tibial nerve S1-3
muscles.action: Abducts fifth toe at metatarsophalangeal joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Foot stability during locomotion.
muscles.injury_risks: Constrictive narrow toe-box shoes.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Sole of the Foot - Second Layer
muscles.latin_origin: quadratus (squared), plantae (of the sole)
muscles.origin: Medial surface of calcaneus and lateral process of calcaneal tuberosity.
muscles.insertion: Lateral border of tendon of flexor digitorum longus in proximal sole of foot.
muscles.nerve: Lateral plantar nerve from tibial nerve S1-3
muscles.action: Flexes distal phalanges of second to fifth toes. Modifies oblique line of pull of flexor digitorum longus.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Holding a pencil between toes and ball of foot.
muscles.injury_risks: Sudden acceleration without adequate arch support.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Sole of the Foot - Second Layer
muscles.latin_origin: lumbricus (earthworm)
muscles.origin: First lumbrical: medial side of tendon of FDL (second toe). Second to fourth: adjacent tendons of FDL.
muscles.insertion: Medial free margins of extensor hoods of second to fifth toes.
muscles.nerve: First lumbrical: medial plantar nerve. Lateral three: lateral plantar nerve S2, 3
muscles.action: Flex metatarsophalangeal joint and extend interphalangeal joints.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Gathering up material under the foot using toes only.
muscles.injury_risks: Forced toe hyperextension.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Sole of the Foot - Third Layer
muscles.latin_origin: flectere (to bend), hallucis (of great toe), brevis (short)
muscles.origin: Medial part of plantar surface of cuboid, adjacent part of lateral cuneiform, tendon of tibialis posterior.
muscles.insertion: Lateral and medial sides of base of proximal phalanx of great toe.
muscles.nerve: Medial plantar nerve from tibial nerve S1, 2
muscles.action: Flexes metatarsophalangeal joint of great toe.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Helping to gather up material under foot involving great toe.
muscles.injury_risks: Turf toe (hyperextension injury of the first MTP joint).

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Sole of the Foot - Third Layer
muscles.latin_origin: adducere (to lead to), hallucis (of great toe)
muscles.origin: Transverse head: ligaments associated with MTP joints of lateral three toes. Oblique head: bases of 2nd-4th metatarsals.
muscles.insertion: Lateral side of base of proximal phalanx of great toe.
muscles.nerve: Lateral plantar nerve from tibial nerve S2, 3
muscles.action: Adducts great toe at metatarsophalangeal joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Making a space between the great toe and adjacent toe.
muscles.injury_risks: Tight footwear squeezing metatarsals together.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Sole of the Foot - Third Layer
muscles.latin_origin: flectere (to bend), digiti (of toe), minimi (smallest), brevis (short)
muscles.origin: Base of fifth metatarsal and sheath of fibularis longus tendon.
muscles.insertion: Lateral side of base of proximal phalanx of little toe.
muscles.nerve: Lateral plantar nerve from tibial nerve S2, 3
muscles.action: Flexes little toe at metatarsophalangeal joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Works alongside other toes to gather up material under foot.
muscles.injury_risks: Lateral foot impact.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Sole of the Foot - Fourth Layer
muscles.latin_origin: dorsalis (relating to back), interosseus (between bones)
muscles.origin: Sides of adjacent metatarsals.
muscles.insertion: Extensor hoods and bases of proximal phalanges of second to fourth toes.
muscles.nerve: Lateral plantar nerve S2, 3 (first & second also innervated by deep fibular nerve).
muscles.action: Abduct second to fourth toes at MTP joints. Resist extension of MTP joints and flexion of IP joints.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Facilitate walking.
muscles.injury_risks: Metatarsal compression injuries.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Sole of the Foot - Fourth Layer
muscles.latin_origin: plantaris (relating to sole), interosseus (between bones)
muscles.origin: Bases and medial sides of third to fifth metatarsals.
muscles.insertion: Extensor hoods and bases of proximal phalanges of third to fifth toes.
muscles.nerve: Lateral plantar nerve from tibial nerve S2, 3
muscles.action: Adduct third to fifth toes at MTP joints. Resist extension of MTP joints and flexion of IP joints.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Facilitate walking.
muscles.injury_risks: High impact forefoot landing.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Anterior Compartment of the Forearm - Intermediate Layer
muscles.latin_origin: flectere (to bend); digitorum (of the fingers/toes); superficialis (on the surface)
muscles.origin: Humero-ulnar head: medial epicondyle of humerus. Adjacent border of coronoid process. Radial head: oblique line of radius.
muscles.insertion: Four tendons each divide into two slips, each of which insert into the sides of the middle phalanges of the four fingers.
muscles.action: Flexes proximal interphalangeal joints of the index, middle, ring, and little fingers; can also flex metacarpophalangeal joints of the same fingers and the wrist joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Examples: 'hook grip,' 'power grip' (as in turning a tap), typing, playing the piano and some stringed instruments.
muscles.injury_risks: Over-extending the wrist as a result of breaking a fall with the hand.
common_problems: Golfer's elbow (overuse tendonitis of the common flexor origin)

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Anterior Compartment of the Forearm - Deep Layer
muscles.latin_origin: flectere (to bend); digitorum (of the fingers/toes); profundus (deep)
muscles.origin: Medial and anterior surfaces of ulna. Medial half of interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Four tendons, which attach to the palmar surfaces of the distal phalanges of the index, middle, ring, and little fingers.
muscles.nerve: Medial half of muscle (destined for little and ring fingers): ulnar nerve C8, T1. Lateral half of muscle (destined for index and middle fingers): anterior interosseous branch of median nerve C8, T1.
muscles.action: Flexes distal interphalangeal joints of the index, middle, ring, and little fingers; can also flex metacarpophalangeal joints of the same fingers and the wrist joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Example: 'hook grip,' as in carrying a briefcase.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Anterior Compartment of the Forearm - Deep Layer
muscles.latin_origin: flectere (to bend); pollicis (of the thumb); longus (long)
muscles.origin: Anterior surface of shaft of radius. Radial half of interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Palmar surface of base of distal phalanx of thumb.
muscles.nerve: Anterior interosseous branch of median nerve C(6), 7, 8.
muscles.action: Flexes interphalangeal joint of thumb. Assists in flexion of metacarpophalangeal joint of thumb.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Examples: picking up small objects between the thumb and fingers, maintaining a firm grip on a hammer.
muscles.injury_risks: Over-extending the wrist as a result of breaking a fall with the hand.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Anterior Compartment of the Forearm - Deep Layer
muscles.latin_origin: pronare (to bend forward); quadratus (squared)
muscles.origin: Linear ridge on distal anterior surface of ulna.
muscles.insertion: Distal anterior surface of radius.
muscles.nerve: Anterior interosseous branch of median nerve C7, 8.
muscles.action: Pronates forearm and hand. Helps hold radius and ulna together, reducing stress on inferior radioulnar joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Example: turning the hand downward, as in pouring a substance out of the hand.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Posterior Compartment of the Forearm - Superficial Layer
muscles.latin_origin: brachium (arm); radius (staff, spoke of wheel)
muscles.origin: Proximal part of lateral supracondylar ridge of humerus and adjacent intermuscular septum.
muscles.insertion: Lower surface of distal end of radius, just above styloid process.
muscles.action: Accessory flexor of elbow joint when forearm is midpronated.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Example: turning a corkscrew.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Posterior Compartment of the Forearm - Superficial Layer
muscles.latin_origin: extendere (to extend); carpi (of the wrist); radius (staff, spoke of wheel); longus (long)
muscles.origin: Distal part of lateral supracondylar ridge of humerus and adjacent intermuscular septum.
muscles.insertion: Dorsal surface of base of second metacarpal.
muscles.action: Extends and abducts wrist.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Examples: kneading dough, typing.
muscles.injury_risks: Over-flexing the wrist as a result of falling onto the hand.
common_problems: Tennis elbow (overuse tendonitis of the common origin on the lateral epicondyle of the humerus)

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Posterior Compartment of the Forearm - Superficial Layer
muscles.latin_origin: extendere (to extend); carpi (of the wrist); radius (staff, spoke of wheel); brevis (short)
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of humerus and adjacent intermuscular septum.
muscles.insertion: Dorsal surface of base of second and third metacarpals.
muscles.action: Extends and abducts wrist.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Examples: kneading dough, typing.
muscles.injury_risks: Over-flexing the wrist as a result of falling onto the hand.
common_problems: Tennis elbow (overuse tendonitis of the common origin on the lateral epicondyle of the humerus)

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Posterior Compartment of the Forearm - Superficial Layer
muscles.latin_origin: extendere (to extend); digitorum (of the fingers/toes)
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of humerus and adjacent intermuscular septum and deep fascia.
muscles.insertion: Four tendons, which insert via extensor hoods into the dorsal aspects of the bases of the middle and distal phalanges of the index, middle, ring, and little fingers.
muscles.action: Extends the index, middle, ring, and little fingers; can also extend the wrist.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Example: letting go of objects held in the hand.
muscles.injury_risks: Over-flexing the wrist as a result of falling onto the hand.
common_problems: Tennis elbow (overuse tendonitis of the common origin on the lateral epicondyle of the humerus)

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Posterior Compartment of the Forearm - Superficial Layer
muscles.latin_origin: extendere (to extend); digiti (of the finger/toe); minimi (of the smallest)
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of humerus and adjacent intermuscular septum together with extensor digitorum.
muscles.insertion: Extensor hood of little finger.
muscles.action: Extends little finger.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Extending the little finger independently.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Posterior Compartment of the Forearm - Superficial Layer
muscles.latin_origin: extendere (to extend); carpi (of the wrist); ulnaris (relating to the elbow/arm)
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of humerus and posterior border of ulna.
muscles.insertion: Tubercle on base of medial side of fifth metacarpal.
muscles.action: Extends and adducts wrist.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Example: cleaning windows.
muscles.injury_risks: Over-flexing the wrist as a result of falling onto the hand.
common_problems: Tennis elbow (overuse tendonitis of the common origin on the lateral epicondyle of the humerus)

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Posterior Compartment of the Forearm - Superficial Layer
muscles.latin_origin: agkon (elbow)
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of humerus.
muscles.insertion: Lateral surface of olecranon process and proximal posterior surface of ulna.
muscles.action: Abduction of ulna in pronation. Accessory extensor of elbow joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Example: pushing objects at arm's length.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Posterior Compartment of the Forearm - Deep Layer
muscles.latin_origin: supinus (lying on the back)
muscles.origin: Superficial part: lateral epicondyle of humerus, radial collateral and anular ligaments. Deep part: supinator crest of ulna.
muscles.insertion: Lateral surface of radius superior to the anterior oblique line.
muscles.action: Supination.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Example: turning a door handle or screwdriver.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Posterior Compartment of the Forearm - Deep Layer
muscles.latin_origin: abducere (to lead away from); pollicis (of the thumb); longus (long)
muscles.origin: Posterior surfaces of ulna and radius, distal to attachments of supinator and anconeus. Intervening interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Lateral side of base of first metacarpal.
muscles.action: Abducts carpometacarpal joint of thumb; accessory extensor of thumb.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Example: releasing the grip on a flat object.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Posterior Compartment of the Forearm - Deep Layer
muscles.latin_origin: extendere (to extend); pollicis (of the thumb); brevis (short)
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of radius, distal to origin of abductor pollicis longus. Adjacent interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Base of dorsal surface of proximal phalanx of thumb.
muscles.action: Extends metacarpophalangeal joint of thumb. Can also extend carpometacarpal joint of thumb.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Example: releasing the grip on a flat object.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Posterior Compartment of the Forearm - Deep Layer
muscles.latin_origin: extendere (to extend); pollicis (of the thumb); longus (long)
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of ulna, distal to abductor pollicis longus. Adjacent interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Dorsal surface of base of distal phalanx of thumb.
muscles.action: Extends interphalangeal joint of thumb. Can also extend carpometacarpal and metacarpophalangeal joint of thumb.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Example: giving the 'thumbs up' gesture.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Posterior Compartment of the Forearm - Deep Layer
muscles.latin_origin: extendere (to extend); indicis (of the index finger)
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of ulna, distal to extensor pollicis longus. Adjacent interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Extensor hood of index finger.
muscles.action: Extends index finger.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Example: pointing at something.
muscles.injury_risks: Repetitive strain from isolated index finger extension.

muscles.anatomical_region: Postvertebral Muscles—Transversospinales Group
muscles.latin_origin: semispinalis, half-spinal; thoracis, of the chest; cervicis, of the neck; capitis, of the head.
muscles.origin: Thoracis: transverse processes of T6–10. Cervicis: transverse processes of T1–6. Capitis: transverse processes of C4–T7.
muscles.insertion: Thoracis: spinous processes of C6–T4. Cervicis: spinous processes of C2–5. Capitis: between superior and inferior nuchal lines of occipital bone.
muscles.nerve: Dorsal rami of thoracic and cervical spinal nerves.
muscles.action: Extends head, neck, and thoracic spine. Rotates head, neck, and thoracic spine to opposite side.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Looking up, extending neck and back, rotating upper spine.
muscles.injury_risks: Heavy lifting with flexed spine or sudden neck rotation.

muscles.anatomical_region: Abdominal Wall
muscles.latin_origin: transversus (across, crosswise); abdominis (of the belly/stomach).
muscles.origin: Anterior two-thirds of iliac crest, lateral third of inguinal ligament, thoracolumbar fascia, and costal cartilages of lower six ribs.
muscles.insertion: Aponeurosis ending in linea alba, pubic crest, and pectineal line.
muscles.nerve: Ventral rami of thoracic spinal nerves T7–12 and L1.
muscles.action: Compresses abdominal contents, stabilizes lumbar spine and pelvis.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Bracing the core, maintaining posture, forced exhalation.
muscles.injury_risks: Lifting heavy without bracing core properly.

muscles.anatomical_region: Posterior Triangle of the Neck
muscles.latin_origin: Greek, skalenos, uneven. Latin, anterior, at the front; medius, middle; posterior, at the back.
muscles.origin: Anterior: anterior tubercles of transverse processes of C3–6. Middle: transverse processes of C2–7. Posterior: posterior tubercles of transverse processes of C4–6.
muscles.insertion: Anterior: scalene tubercle and upper surface of 1st rib. Middle: upper surface of 1st rib, behind groove for subclavian artery. Posterior: upper surface of 2nd rib.
muscles.nerve: Anterior: C4–7 ventral rami. Middle: C3–7 ventral rami. Posterior: C5–7 ventral rami.
muscles.action: Bilateral: flex neck; raise 1st or 2nd rib during active respiration. Unilateral: side flex and rotate head.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Accessory muscle of respiration; side flexes and rotates head.
sports_heavy_utilization: All active endurance sports requiring heavy respiration
muscles.injury_risks: Tightness compressing brachial plexus nerves or subclavian artery.
common_problems: Pain in neck, shoulder, and arm
Thoracic outlet syndrome / brachial plexus compression

muscles.anatomical_region: Posterior / Anterior Neck Regions
muscles.latin_origin: Greek, sternon, chest; kleis, key/clavicle; mastoides, breast shaped.
muscles.origin: Sternal head: upper part of anterior surface of manubrium. Clavicular head: upper surface of medial third of clavicle.
muscles.insertion: Sternal head: lateral superior nuchal line of occipital bone. Clavicular head: outer surface of mastoid process.
muscles.nerve: Accessory nerve (Cranial Nerve XI) and C2-C3 ventral rami.
muscles.action: Bilateral: pulls head forward, lifts sternum/ribcage during deep breathing. Unilateral: lateral flexion to same side; rotates head to opposite side.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Looking over shoulder, lifting head off pillow, assisting deep inhalation.
muscles.injury_risks: Whiplash injuries from rapid acceleration/deceleration.

muscles.anatomical_region: Postvertebral Muscles — Erector Spinae Group (Lateral Column)
muscles.latin_origin: ilio (relating to the ilium/hipbone); costalis (relating to the ribs).
muscles.origin: Sacrum, lumbar and lower thoracic spinous processes, supraspinous ligaments, iliac crest, and upper rib angles.
muscles.insertion: Angles of lower and upper ribs, and transverse processes of lower cervical vertebrae (C4–C7).
muscles.nerve: Dorsal rami of cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spinal nerves (C4–S5).
muscles.action: Extends spine, side-flexes trunk, assists with rib depression during forced exhalation.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Maintaining upright posture, arching back, side bending.
muscles.injury_risks: Lifting heavy loads with improper spinal alignment.

muscles.anatomical_region: Postvertebral Muscles — Erector Spinae Group (Intermediate Column)
muscles.latin_origin: longissimus (longest).
muscles.origin: Lumbar transverse processes, upper thoracic transverse processes (T1–T5), and lower cervical articular processes (C4–C7).
muscles.insertion: Thoracic/lumbar transverse processes, lower rib angles, cervical transverse processes (C2–C6), and mastoid process.
muscles.action: Extends and laterally flexes spine; assists rib depression during forceful breathing; extends and rotates head (capitis).
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Postural stabilization, extending back, turning head.
muscles.injury_risks: Vulnerable during improper lifting techniques or sudden twisting under strain.

muscles.anatomical_region: Postvertebral Muscles — Erector Spinae Group (Medial Column)
muscles.latin_origin: spinalis (relating to the spine).
muscles.origin: Spinous processes of upper lumbar (L1–L2) and lower thoracic (T11–T12) vertebrae, ligamentum nuchae, and C7 spinous process.
muscles.insertion: Upper thoracic spinous processes (T1–T8), C2 spinous process, and occipital attachments.
muscles.action: Extends the vertebral column to maintain erect posture; extends head (capitis).
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Seated and standing erect posture, arching spine.
muscles.injury_risks: Strain from lifting heavy objects without bending at hips and knees.

muscles.anatomical_region: Anterior Compartment of the Thigh
muscles.latin_origin: Latin, sartor, tailor.
muscles.origin: Anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS).
muscles.insertion: Medial surface of tibia just inferomedial to tibial tuberosity.
muscles.action: Flexes the thigh at the hip joint. Flexes the leg at the knee joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Sitting cross-legged.
muscles.injury_risks: Overambitious yoga exercises in cross-legged or lotus positions.
common_problems: Pain or damage to the inside of the knee.

muscles.muscle_name: Quadriceps (Rectus Femoris, Vastus Lateralis, Vastus Medialis, Vastus Intermedius)
muscles.anatomical_region: Anterior Compartment of the Thigh
muscles.latin_origin: Latin, rectus, straight; femoris, of the thigh; vastus, vast; lateralis, relating to the side.
muscles.origin: Rectus femoris: AIIS & groove above acetabulum. Vasti group: upper half of shaft of femur.
muscles.insertion: Patella, then via patellar ligament into the tibial tuberosity.
muscles.action: Rectus femoris flexes thigh at hip and extends leg at knee. Vasti group extends leg at knee.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Walking up stairs, sitting down, climbing, cycling.
muscles.injury_risks: Patellofemoral maltracking, improper knee alignment under heavy loading.

muscles.anatomical_region: Medial Compartment of the Thigh
muscles.latin_origin: Latin, adducere, to lead to; magnus, large; brevis, small; longus, long; gracilis, slender.
muscles.origin: Anterior surface of pubic bone, inferior pubic ramus, ramus of ischium, and ischial tuberosity.
muscles.insertion: Linea aspera, medial supracondylar line, and adductor tubercle of femur; medial proximal tibia (gracilis).
muscles.nerve: Obturator nerve L2, 3, 4 (and Tibial division of Sciatic nerve for Magnus).
muscles.action: Adducts and medially rotates thigh at hip joint; flexes leg at knee joint (Gracilis).
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Bringing the second leg in or out of a car; sitting with knees pressed together.
muscles.injury_risks: Side splits or high side kicks without sufficient warm-up.
common_problems: Groin pulls (tends to be tighter in men than in women).

muscles.anatomical_region: Posterior Compartment of the Thigh
muscles.latin_origin: Latin, semi, half; membranosus, membranous; tendinosus, tendinous; biceps, two-headed.
muscles.origin: Ischial tuberosity. Biceps femoris short head: lateral lip of linea aspera.
muscles.insertion: Head of fibula (Biceps femoris); medial tibial condyle/proximal tibia (Semimembranosus/Semitendinosus).
muscles.action: Flexes leg at knee joint; extends thigh at hip joint; rotates leg at knee joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Slowing down the leg at the end of forward swing during running; controlling trunk forward flexion.
muscles.injury_risks: Sudden lengthening without warm-up (e.g., forward kicking, splits).

muscles.muscle_name: Anterior Leg Extensors (Extensor Digitorum Longus, Extensor Hallucis Longus, Fibularis Tertius)
muscles.anatomical_region: Anterior Compartment of the Leg
muscles.latin_origin: Latin, extendere, to extend; digitorum, of toes; hallucis, of great toe; fibula, pin; tertius, third.
muscles.origin: Medial surface of fibula, lateral tibial condyle, and interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Dorsal surfaces of digits 2–5, base of distal phalanx of great toe, dorsomedial surface of 5th metatarsal base.
muscles.action: Dorsiflexes foot, everts foot, extends toes and great toe.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Walking up stairs (ensuring toes clear steps).
muscles.injury_risks: Tendon compression bruising (toe stepped on) or forced ankle inversion.
common_problems: Ankle instability from forced inversion injuries

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Hand
muscles.latin_origin: Latin, palmaris, relating to the palm; brevis, short.
muscles.origin: Palmar aponeurosis. Flexor retinaculum.
muscles.insertion: Skin on ulnar border of hand.
muscles.nerve: Superficial branch of ulnar nerve C(7), 8, T1.
muscles.action: Improves grip.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: A small subcutaneous muscle lying over the hypothenar eminence that improves grip.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Hand
muscles.latin_origin: Latin, dorsalis, relating to the back; interosseus, between bones.
muscles.origin: By two heads, each from adjacent sides of metacarpals.
muscles.insertion: Extensor hood and base of proximal phalanges of index, middle, and ring fingers.
muscles.nerve: Deep branch of ulnar nerve C8, T1.
muscles.action: Abduction of index, middle, and ring fingers at metacarpophalangeal joints.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Spreading the fingers as if to indicate numbers from two to four.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Hand
muscles.latin_origin: Latin, palmaris, relating to the palm; interosseus, between bones.
muscles.origin: Sides of metacarpals.
muscles.insertion: Extensor hoods of the thumb, index, ring, and little fingers and proximal phalanx of thumb.
muscles.nerve: Deep branch of ulnar nerve C8, T1.
muscles.action: Adduction of the thumb, index, ring, and little fingers at metacarpophalangeal joints.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Cupping the hand as if to retain water in the palm (i.e. drinking from the hand).

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Hand
muscles.latin_origin: Latin, adducere, to lead to; pollicis, of the thumb.
muscles.origin: Transverse head: palmar surface of third metacarpal. Oblique head: capitate and bases of second and third metacarpals.
muscles.insertion: Base of proximal phalanx of thumb and extensor hood of thumb.
muscles.nerve: Deep branch of ulnar nerve C8, T1.
muscles.action: Adducts thumb.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Gripping a jam jar lid to screw it on.
muscles.injury_risks: Over-abducting the thumb as a result of falling onto the hand.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Hand
muscles.latin_origin: Latin, lumbricus, earthworm.
muscles.origin: Tendons of flexor digitorum profundus.
muscles.insertion: Extensor hoods of index, ring, middle, and little fingers.
muscles.nerve: Lateral lumbricals (first and second): digital branches of median nerve. Medial lumbricals (third and fourth): deep branch of ulnar nerve.
muscles.action: Extend interphalangeal joints and simultaneously flex metacarpophalangeal joints.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Cupping the hand.
common_problems: Inability to maintain flexion of the interphalangeal joints, as in rock climbing

muscles.muscle_name: Hypothenar Eminence (Abductor Digiti Minimi, Flexor Digiti Minimi Brevis, Opponens Digiti Minimi)
muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Hand—Hypothenar Eminence
muscles.latin_origin: Latin, abducere, to lead away from; digiti, of the finger/toe; minimi, of the smallest; flectere, to flex; brevis, short; opponens, opposing.
muscles.origin: Abductor: Pisiform, pisohamate ligament, and tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris. Flexor & Opponens: Hook of hamate, Flexor retinaculum.
muscles.insertion: Proximal phalanx of little finger (Abductor & Flexor); Entire length of medial (ulnar) border of fifth metacarpal (Opponens).
muscles.nerve: Deep branch of ulnar nerve C(7), 8, T1.
muscles.action: Abducts, flexes, and opposes the little finger at the metacarpophalangeal joint; laterally rotates fifth metacarpal.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Holding a thread within the fingertips (along with the other fingertips); holding a large ball.
muscles.injury_risks: Over-abducting or over-extending the little finger as a result of falling onto the ulnar side of the hand.

muscles.muscle_name: Thenar Eminence (Abductor Pollicis Brevis, Flexor Pollicis Brevis, Opponens Pollicis)
muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Hand—Thenar Eminence
muscles.latin_origin: Latin, abducere, to lead away from; pollicis, of the thumb; brevis, short; flectere, to flex; opponens, opposing.
muscles.origin: Tubercles of trapezium and scaphoid, flexor retinaculum.
muscles.insertion: Proximal phalanx and extensor hood of thumb; entire length of radial border of first metacarpal.
muscles.nerve: Recurrent branch of median nerve C8, T1.
muscles.action: Abducts, flexes, and medially rotates thumb at metacarpophalangeal joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Picking up a small object between the thumb and fingers; typing; holding a thread between the thumb and fingertips.
muscles.injury_risks: Over-extending the thumb as a result of falling onto the hand.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Gluteal Region
muscles.latin_origin: Greek, gloutos, buttock. Latin, maximus, biggest.
muscles.origin: Fascia covering gluteus medius, external surface of ilium behind posterior gluteal line, fascia of erector spinae, dorsal surface of lower sacrum, lateral margin of coccyx, external surface of sacrotuberous ligament.
muscles.insertion: Posterior aspect of iliotibial band of fascia lata; Gluteal tuberosity of proximal femur.
muscles.action: Powerful extensor of flexed femur at hip joint. Lateral stabilizer of hip and knee joints. Laterally rotates and abducts thigh.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Walking upstairs, rising from sitting.
muscles.injury_risks: Pelvic imbalances.
common_problems: Pain in the hips, low back, and lateral area of the knees.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Gluteal Region
muscles.latin_origin: Latin, tendere, to stretch, pull; fasciae, of the band; latae, of the broad.
muscles.origin: Lateral aspect of crest of ilium between ASIS and tubercle of the crest.
muscles.insertion: Iliotibial band of fascia lata.
muscles.action: Stabilizes the knee in extension.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Walking.
muscles.injury_risks: Pelvic imbalances.
common_problems: Pain in the hips, low back, and lateral area of the knees.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Gluteal Region
muscles.latin_origin: Greek, gloutos, buttock. Latin, medius, middle; minimus, smallest.
muscles.origin: External surface of ilium between anterior and posterior gluteal lines (Medius); external surface of ilium between anterior and inferior gluteal lines (Minimus).
muscles.insertion: Oblique ridge on lateral surface of greater trochanter (Medius); anterolateral border of greater trochanter (Minimus).
muscles.action: Abducts femur at hip joint. Medially rotates thigh. Holds pelvis secure over stance leg and prevents pelvic drop on opposite swing side during walking (Trendelenburg gait).
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Stepping sideways over an object, such as a low fence.
muscles.injury_risks: Pelvic imbalances.
common_problems: Pain in the hips, low back, and knees.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Gluteal Region
muscles.latin_origin: Latin, pirum, pear; forma, shape.
muscles.origin: Anterior surface of sacrum between anterior sacral foramina.
muscles.insertion: Medial side of superior border of greater trochanter.
muscles.action: Laterally rotates extended femur at hip joint. Abducts flexed femur at hip joint. Helps hold head of femur in acetabulum.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Bringing the first leg out of a car.
muscles.injury_risks: Tight piriformis squeezing the sciatic nerve.
common_problems: Piriformis syndrome (sciatic pain that begins in the buttocks).

muscles.muscle_name: Deep Lateral Hip Rotators (Obturator Internus, Gemellus Superior, Gemellus Inferior, Quadratus Femoris)
muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Gluteal Region—Deep Lateral Hip Rotators
muscles.latin_origin: Latin, obturare, to obstruct; internus, internal; gemellus, twin/double; superior, upper; inferior, lower; quadratus, squared; femoris, of the thigh.
muscles.origin: Anterolateral wall of true pelvis (Obturator internus); external surface of ischial spine (Gemellus sup.); upper aspect of ischial tuberosity (Gemellus inf.); lateral edge of ischium (Quadratus femoris).
muscles.insertion: Medial side of greater trochanter / intertrochanteric crest of proximal femur.
muscles.nerve: Nerve to obturator internus L5, S1; Nerve to quadratus femoris L5, S1, (2).
muscles.action: Laterally rotate hip joint. Abduct flexed femur at hip joint. Help hold head of femur in acetabulum.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Bringing the first leg out of a car.
muscles.injury_risks: Chronically tight muscles.
common_problems: Person stands with the feet turned out.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Shoulder
muscles.latin_origin: deltoides, shaped like the Greek capital letter delta (Δ)
muscles.origin: Anterior fibers: anterior border of lateral one-third of clavicle. Middle fibers: lateral margin of acromion process. Posterior fibers: inferior edge of crest of spine of scapula.
muscles.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity of humerus
muscles.action: Major abductor of the arm (abducts arm beyond initial 15 degrees, which is done by supraspinatus); anterior fibers assist in flexing the arm; posterior fibers assist in extending the arm.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Reaching for something out to the side, raising the arm to wave.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Shoulder — Rotator Cuff
muscles.latin_origin: supra, above; spina, spine
muscles.origin: Medial two-thirds of supraspinous fossa of scapula and deep fascia that covers the muscle.
muscles.insertion: Most superior facet on the greater tubercle of humerus
muscles.action: Initiates abduction of arm to 15 degrees at glenohumeral joint (at which point deltoid takes over).
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Holding a shopping bag away from the side of the body.
muscles.injury_risks: Dislocation of the glenohumeral joint.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Shoulder — Rotator Cuff
muscles.latin_origin: infra, below; spina, spine
muscles.origin: Medial two-thirds of infraspinous fossa of scapula and deep fascia that covers the muscle.
muscles.insertion: Middle facet on posterior surface of greater tubercle of humerus
muscles.action: Lateral rotation of arm at glenohumeral joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Brushing back hair.
muscles.injury_risks: Dislocation of the glenohumeral joint.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Shoulder — Rotator Cuff
muscles.latin_origin: teres, rounded, finely shaped; minor, smaller
muscles.origin: Upper two-thirds of a strip of bone on posterior surface of scapula immediately adjacent to lateral border of scapula.
muscles.insertion: Inferior facet on greater tubercle of humerus
muscles.action: Lateral rotation of arm at glenohumeral joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Brushing back hair.
muscles.injury_risks: Dislocation of the glenohumeral joint.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Shoulder — Rotator Cuff
muscles.latin_origin: sub, under; scapularis, relating to the shoulder blade
muscles.origin: Medial two-thirds of subscapular fossa.
muscles.insertion: Lesser tubercle of humerus
muscles.nerve: Upper and lower subscapular nerves C5, 6, (7)
muscles.action: Medial rotation of arm at glenohumeral joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Reaching into the back pocket.
muscles.injury_risks: Twisting the arm behind the back (as in an overzealous restraining hold), or struggling to free oneself from that position.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Anterior Compartment of the Arm
muscles.latin_origin: biceps, two-headed; brachii, of the arm
muscles.origin: Long head: supraglenoid tubercle of scapula. Short head: tip of coracoid process.
muscles.insertion: Radial tuberosity
muscles.action: Powerful flexor of forearm at elbow joint. Supinates forearm. Accessory flexor of arm at glenohumeral joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Picking up an object, bringing food to the mouth.
muscles.injury_risks: Lifting heavy objects too quickly.
common_problems: Flexion deformity of the elbow (elbow cannot be fully straightened)

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Anterior Compartment of the Arm
muscles.latin_origin: brachialis, relating to the arm
muscles.origin: Anterior aspect of humerus (medial and lateral surfaces) and adjacent intermuscular septae.
muscles.insertion: Tuberosity of ulna
muscles.nerve: Musculocutaneous nerve C5, 6. Small contribution by radial nerve (C7) to lateral part of muscle.
muscles.action: Powerful flexor of forearm at elbow joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Bringing food to the mouth.
common_problems: Flexion deformity of the elbow (elbow cannot be fully straightened)

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Anterior Compartment of the Arm
muscles.latin_origin: korakoeides, raven-like; brachialis, relating to the arm
muscles.origin: Tip of coracoid process.
muscles.insertion: Medial aspect of humerus at mid-shaft.
muscles.action: Flexor of arm at glenohumeral joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Mopping the floor.
muscles.injury_risks: Suddenly hitting the ground when swinging the bat hard in cricket.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Posterior Compartment of the Arm
muscles.latin_origin: triceps, three-headed; brachii, of the arm
muscles.origin: Long head: infraglenoid tubercle of scapula. Medial head: posterior surface of humerus (below and medial to radial groove). Lateral head: posterior surface of humerus (above and lateral to radial groove).
muscles.insertion: Posterior part of olecranon process of ulna.
muscles.action: Extends forearm at elbow joint. Long head can also extend and adduct arm at shoulder joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Throwing objects, pushing a door shut.
muscles.injury_risks: Throwing with excessive force.
common_problems: Extension deformity of elbow (elbow cannot be fully flexed)

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Anterior Compartment of the Forearm — Superficial Layer
muscles.latin_origin: flectere, to bend; carpi, of the wrist; ulnaris, relating to the elbow/arm
muscles.origin: Humeral head: medial epicondyle of humerus. Ulnar head: medial border of olecranon and posterior border of upper two-thirds of ulna.
muscles.insertion: Pisiform bone. Hook of hamate. Base of fifth metacarpal.
muscles.action: Flexes and adducts wrist.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Pulling an object toward you.
muscles.injury_risks: Over-extending the wrist as a result of breaking a fall with the hand.
common_problems: Golfer's elbow (overuse tendonitis of the common flexor origin)

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Anterior Compartment of the Forearm — Superficial Layer
muscles.latin_origin: palmaris, relating to the palm; longus, long
muscles.origin: Medial epicondyle of humerus.
muscles.insertion: Palmar aponeurosis of hand.
muscles.action: Flexes wrist joint. Tenses palmar fascia.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Grasping a small ball, cupping the palm to drink from the hand.

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Anterior Compartment of the Forearm — Superficial Layer
muscles.latin_origin: flectere, to bend; carpi, of the wrist; radius, staff, spoke of wheel
muscles.origin: Medial epicondyle of humerus.
muscles.insertion: Bases of second and third metacarpals.
muscles.action: Flexes and abducts wrist joint.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Pulling rope in toward you, wielding an axe or hammer.
muscles.injury_risks: Over-extending the wrist as a result of breaking a fall with the hand.
common_problems: Golfer's elbow (overuse tendonitis of the common flexor origin)

muscles.anatomical_region: Muscles of the Anterior Compartment of the Forearm — Superficial Layer
muscles.latin_origin: pronare, to bend forward; teres, rounded, finely shaped
muscles.origin: Humeral head: medial epicondyle and adjacent supra-epicondylar ridge. Ulnar head: medial border of coronoid process.
muscles.insertion: Mid-lateral surface of radius (pronator tuberosity).
muscles.action: Pronates forearm.
muscles.basic_functional_movement: Pouring liquid from a container, turning a doorknob.
